open_obligations: Check whether LLM and human judges err on the same items, not only at similar rates.
Note that persona-aware debaters change the comparison.
Check whether the equivalence holds on Kenton et al.'s extractive and closed tasks.
in.other_title: Persona-conditioned GPT-4o judges of debate reach 78.5% vs 70.1% for human judges
in.rationale: Kenton et al. state their study is limited by using LLM judges instead of humans. Rahman et al. compare both and report default GPT-4o (69.8%) and Qwen2.5-7B (70.7%) debate judges are comparable to human judges (70.1%), while persona-based GPT-4o judges are higher (up to 78.5%); this is one domain with GPT-4o debaters.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether LLM judges are a reasonable stand-in for human judges of debate, on COVID-19 claims

text: The authors state the study is limited by not using humans and by using AI that is far from superhuman on many capabilities, and name as a key uncertainty whether humans will be able to follow and accurately judge arguments made by superhuman AI.
title: LLM judges stand in for humans and agents are not superhuman
